changes.basisRationale: Restore NIH ODS/FNB adult35 mg/day UL for added niacin from supplements and fortified foods. This is niacin mass, not dietary niacin equivalents from tryptophan. Generic supplemental reporting cannot verify unquantified fortified-food exposure.
changes.safetyNotes: Flushing is especially associated with nicotinic acid; nicotinamide has a different adverse-effect profile. The FNB added-niacin UL covers both forms. Liver and other risks depend on form, amount and duration. Unknown added-food niacin prevents a complete exposure claim.

evidence.reference: Adult35 mg/day niacin added in supplements and fortified foods, covering nicotinic acid and nicotinamide; natural food niacin and tryptophan equivalents are outside this UL.
evidence.scopeLimitation: Supplemental scope quantifies continued/new supplements; the present intake model cannot isolate added niacin from unspecified food. Fortified-food exposure remains uncertainty, never assumed zero.
